column1: # Compound identities for Zhuo et al. 2026.
# Verification status per row, in notes:
#   ligand-verified  matches the deposited chemical component A1C68 in 10PI and 10PJ
#   source-verified  fetched from PubChem and checked against the published formula
#   anchor-derived   built with RDKit molzip from the povorcitinib core, which itself
#                    rebuilds PubChem's povorcitinib exactly, including its stereocentre
#   figure-derived   read from a composite table drawing, with no name or coordinates
# The Table 4, 5 and 6 series (9, 14-22) share one scaffold that differs only in the hinge
# binder, the two aryl fluorines and the amide N-substituent, so all of them are derived
# from the verified povorcitinib core. The Table 1 scaffolds (4-8) change the linker ring
# and the capping group and are read from the drawing.

column8: The first approved JAK inhibitor, dual JAK1/JAK2, shown as the starting point of the field. Structure from PubChem, formula C17H18N6. source-verified.

Dual JAK1/JAK2, approved for rheumatoid arthritis. The azetidine with a cyanomethyl group that this campaign's scaffold also uses is visible here. Structure from PubChem, formula C16H17N7O2S. source-verified.

The company's first JAK1-selective clinical candidate, 21-fold selective, and the benchmark every compound in Table 2 is measured against. Structure from PubChem, formula C26H23F4N9O. source-verified.
The starting scaffold: a urea capping group and poor permeability at 0.1. figure-derived from the Table 1 drawing.
Alkylating the pyrrolidine gives about 20-fold selectivity, matching itacitinib, but the urea keeps the ADME poor. figure-derived.
The urea replaced by an amide on a cyclobutyl: permeability improves to 1.3. figure-derived.
The phenyl amide: better on both enzyme and cell than either the urea or the cyclobutyl. figure-derived.
Piperidine to the more rigid azetidine: three-fold on enzyme and cell, two-fold in whole blood. figure-derived.

The simple isopropyl amide. Clearance improves, potency holds, and whole blood isoform selectivity doubles to 12-fold. Its dog PK is worse than itacitinib's, which is the problem the rest of the paper solves. anchor-derived.
The trifluoromethyl alone, with no ortho-fluorine: almost no effect on permeability or rat PK. The control that shows the two changes only work together. anchor-derived.
The ortho-fluorine alone: Caco-2 up three-fold, rat exposure up four-fold. anchor-derived.
Both together: Caco-2 up five-fold, rat exposure 7.5-fold, and cynomolgus exposure 52-fold over compound 9. anchor-derived.
The meta-fluorine added for potency: three-fold on enzyme and cell over 15. anchor-derived.
INCB047986. The best of this series: 0.25 nM, Caco-2 8.5, excellent in rat and monkey, and 1 per cent oral bioavailability in dog. anchor-derived.

The experiment that proves the hydrogen bond. Identical to 18 except the ortho-fluorine is removed, and Caco-2 falls from 8.5 to 1.4 with rat exposure from 11,884 to 5,606 while potency is unchanged at 0.25 nM. anchor-derived.
The bare pyrazole as hinge binder: it works, at 314 nM. A 1250-fold loss, and the starting point for getting it back. anchor-derived.
One methyl on the pyrazole: 16-fold back. anchor-derived.

Povorcitinib, INCB054707. Both methyls: 28-fold back, 44-fold weaker than 18 on the enzyme, nearly twice as selective, and 100 per cent oral bioavailability in dog against 18's 1 per cent. ligand-verified against A1C68 in both 10PI and 10PJ, and identical to PubChem's povorcitinib including the stereocentre.
